0.11.0.lead: A day now holds more than text and photos: videos, voice recordings, PDFs and links. And photos can be added to older days too.

sections.title: Attachments
sections.body: Below the photos of a day stands the section “Attachments”. With “Attach” you add a video, a PDF or a link. Videos play right in nexdiary, a PDF is leafed through page by page, a link opens only when you tap it; nexdiary itself never visits the page. When you share a day, the attachments go along, like the photos. An HEVC video from an iPhone is converted to H.264 by the server if you like, then it plays everywhere.

sections.title: Add photos to older days
sections.body: The menu “Attach” has “Add photos”, on every day that is not locked. Several at once work, on a phone with the camera too, and from Immich when it is connected. The photos show below the text, the cover stays as it is.

sections.title: Voice recordings
sections.body: Next to the field there is a microphone. You record, give the recording a name and keep it, and it lies with the attachments of the day. In the quick note, today's recordings stand below the notes. A recording lasts at most 30 minutes. The microphone works only when nexdiary runs on https.

small: “My photos” has a tab “Attachments”: every video, recording, PDF and link, filtered by kind, sorted by date or size, to delete. The storage line says how much goes to photos, videos and the rest.
The operator sets under Settings, Attachments how large a video or a PDF may be and whether HEVC videos are converted.
The search finds attachments by their name.

0.10.0.lead: Days gone by can be added now, even without any notes, and written up by the AI from a few words.

sections.title: Add a past day
sections.body: At the top of the journal, next to blog and timeline, stands the button “Add a past day”. You pick a date, yesterday is already chosen, and land in the writing view of that day. This works for a day you noted nothing on, too. If the day already has a page, that page opens to read.

sections.title: Notes while writing
sections.body: Under “Your notes” you can add notes while writing. They belong to the day you are writing, not to today. As soon as the day has notes, “Write it up with AI” is ready, so a day added afterwards becomes a page from a few words.

small: When the browser translates the page, Chrome or Edge for instance, nexdiary keeps working. Until now the whole page could disappear.

0.9.0.lead: The photos of a day now stand as small previews, and HDR photos from an iPhone can be uploaded.

sections.title: Photos as previews with a magnifier
sections.where: Reading a day, a shared day
sections.body: The photos under the text of a day stand in rows of small previews, each in the shape of its photo, upright, wide, square or panorama. A tap opens the big view with the whole picture, where you move through all the photos of the day as before.

sections.title: HDR photos from an iPhone
sections.body: Safari sends an HDR photo as a JPEG that carries a second picture for the brightness. nexdiary took that for something other than a photo and refused it. It is taken now.

small: The previews load the small copy of a photo; the original only in the big view.

0.8.1.lead: A small fix for running behind a reverse proxy.

sections.title: X-Forwarded-Proto only from trusted proxies
sections.where: Settings, Sign-in, Ready for the internet?
sections.body: Whether cookies get the Secure flag and whether “Ready for the internet?” shows https as fine now depends only on a proxy listed in NEXDIARY_TRUSTED_PROXIES. Until now the X-Forwarded-Proto header of any sender counted for this. If nexdiary runs behind a proxy, list it there or set NEXDIARY_COOKIE_SECURE to on; otherwise cookies in auto mode stay without Secure.

small: The https hint in “Ready for the internet?” names NEXDIARY_TRUSTED_PROXIES.

0.8.0.lead: A few numbers about your diary for a dashboard card, read with an API token.

sections.title: Numbers for a dashboard card
sections.body: With an API token, a program such as a dashboard card can ask whether you wrote today, how long your streak is, how many pages and notes this month has and the day your next time capsule opens. Only counts and days: never a text, a title, a value or a tag. The operator switches API tokens on under Settings, API.

small: The hints under “Require a second factor” name the provider switch that exempts a sign-in.

0.7.0.lead: Sign in through several providers at once, each with its own button, set up the same way as in every nex app.

sections.title: Several sign-in providers
sections.body: Add any provider that speaks OpenID Connect: authentik, Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Authelia or Pocket ID, as many as you like. Each gets its own button on the sign-in page and its own redirect address. The provider you had becomes the first entry of the list and keeps working at the address it knew. The authentik button sets authentik up in one step, now with the reason when a step fails, and a blueprint to download instead.

sections.title: Linked by account, never by mail address
sections.body: Link your account to a provider with your password, and unlink it again; a row per provider shows whether it is linked. Somebody who comes through a provider is found only by that link, never by a mail address. New people come by invitation, or as members where the operator switches that on per provider.

sections.title: The second factor per provider
sections.where: Settings, Sign-in, the form of a provider
sections.body: "The provider checks the second factor itself": then a sign-in through it asks for no code of nexdiary's own. Off, whoever has a second factor here gives its code after the provider. An account that signs in through providers only is never made to set one up; an account with a password still is when it signs in with the password. Your provider keeps what it did before: the code is asked unless you had switched that off.

sections.title: Photos of today in two rows
sections.body: "Upload" and, when Immich is set up, "All photos" stay at the top. Below them are the photos that belong to the day, and apart from them the suggestions from Immich. Tap a suggestion to take it; it moves into the first row. Remove the photo again and it goes back to the suggestions.

small: Before the public address changes, nexdiary says which redirect addresses authentik and the providers by hand still know.
Behind a reverse proxy named in NEXDIARY_TRUSTED_PROXIES, nexdiary believes the scheme it reports (X-Forwarded-Proto).
In the list of accounts, the operator sees which providers each account is linked to and can remove a link, with the own password; the person is told.
"Ready for the internet?" names the providers that are trusted with the second factor.
Mails now carry a Date header. Some providers, among them iCloud, Outlook and Gmail, silently dropped mails without one.

0.6.0.lead: Photos from other apps can now be shared to nexdiary.

sections.title: Share photos to nexdiary
sections.where: Share menu on the phone, quick note
sections.body: Share up to 10 photos from the gallery or another app to nexdiary, with a text if you like. Each photo becomes a note of today, the text goes into the first. The photos take the same way as an upload: drawn anew without place and camera data, stored encrypted. If you are not signed in at the moment, they arrive after you sign in. This works with the installed app on Android with Chrome and on Windows with Edge; the iPhone does not offer sharing to web apps.

small: Texts and links from other apps land in the field of the quick note, as before.

0.5.0.lead: Letters that open only on a chosen day, and a few new reasons to keep writing.

sections.title: Time capsules
sections.body: Write a letter to yourself in a year or to someone in the family, or to several at once, written like a page of the diary and with as many photos as you like. Until the day, the people it is for only see who it is from and when it opens. A letter to yourself stays sealed for you too; a letter to others can be changed or taken back until the day. On the morning it opens, a notification arrives on the phone.

sections.title: Looking back on a week or a month
sections.body: The week as a strip of covers, the month as a collage, with your rating as a line, the best day and what it was about. At the press of a button the AI sums the time up in a few sentences.

sections.title: A bookshelf, and a year as a book
sections.body: Every year is a volume that fills up page by page. “As a book” turns a year into a PDF for printing, with a title page, contents, a chapter for each month and a page for each day.

sections.title: Family question
sections.body: One question a day for everyone who joins. You see the others' answers once you have answered yourself, and again later when you read that day. Off at first; each person switches it on for themselves.

sections.title: Just briefly today
sections.body: On tired days without notes, your first rating and one sentence are enough, and the day counts for your streak. You can make more of it later.

small: With “Ask me first”, the AI asks up to two questions about what your notes leave open before it writes. Your answers become notes.
A page can now be deleted, when reading the day and when writing. Your notes and the photos of the day stay.

0.4.0.lead: Notes you add after writing a page now reach the page too.

sections.title: Write it up anew
sections.body: When a day already has a page, the AI can write it anew from all notes, including the ones added later. nexdiary asks first, and nothing is replaced before you save. Not on a locked day.

small: An operator who forgot their own password makes the reset link on the server. The README says how.

0.3.0.lead: Give your pages fixed headings. When the AI writes a page up, it fills them with what your notes say about each.

sections.title: Templates for your pages
sections.body: Create templates with headings, each with a question as a hint, and pick one as your default. Two examples help you get started.

sections.title: The AI fills in only what your notes say
sections.body: When it writes a page up, the AI writes under your headings. A section your notes say nothing about stays empty. Nothing is made up.

sections.title: Writing it yourself, with a frame
sections.body: The headings are already in the text, with the question as a grey hint below. Empty sections are dropped when you save.

small: Writing up in the morning uses your default template, if you have one.

0.2.0.lead: Write as often as suits you. Set a goal for the week, and your streak follows it.

sections.title: Your writing goal
sections.body: Choose how often you want to write, from once to seven times a week. Below seven the streak counts weeks in which you reached your goal, so a day without writing breaks nothing.

sections.title: Shields for your streak
sections.body: A long streak or a long entry earns a shield. It saves your streak over a missed day or a missed week on its own.

sections.title: A reminder when the week runs short
sections.body: If you like, nexdiary reminds you when your goal for the week is getting tight, for example on Friday with two entries still open.

small: The writing page saves its text the same way however quickly you tap Save.

0.1.0.lead: The first version of nexdiary: a diary for the family on your own server. During the day you jot thoughts down in a few words, in the evening they become a page.

sections.title: Note by day, write in the evening
sections.where: Today, and the quick note on the phone
sections.body: Write down what comes to mind, without minding the spelling. In the evening you turn it into a page in the style of a blog, by yourself or with the help of the AI. The notes always stay.

sections.title: A picture for every day
sections.body: Every day has a cover picture: a photo of your own or one of 256 drawn illustrations. A suggestion by season and time of day is already chosen, and you can change it.

sections.title: Values, tags and questions
sections.body: Mood, sleep or whatever else you want to follow, from 1 to 10. Tags too, and small questions of the day for when nothing comes to mind.

sections.title: Journal, search and statistics
sections.body: Browse like a blog or by month, with a search over texts and notes. The statistics show streaks, mood over time and your best and your worst day.

sections.title: Share a day
sections.body: You share single days with people from the family. They can read and give a heart, nothing more. Values and notes go along only if you tick them, and you take a share back at any time.

sections.title: Photos and Immich
sections.body: You upload photos or fetch them from your Immich. Place and shooting data are removed.

sections.title: A reminder by push
sections.body: Daily at your time or only after a few days of pause, with a question if you like.

sections.title: Photos, large and in their place
sections.body: Photos open large and swipe through the day. Put them into the text, choose the part of a cover you want to see, crop or turn an image. My photos shows all of them and where they are used, and deletes what you no longer need.

sections.title: Late nights and days to catch up
sections.body: After midnight nexdiary asks once whether the night still belongs to yesterday. Days with notes but no page yet are listed, so you can write them later, and if you like the AI puts them in order the next morning as a draft that waits for you.

sections.title: Lock a day for good
sections.body: A written day can be locked. After that nobody changes or deletes it any more, you neither.

sections.title: Safe, and yours alone
sections.body: Everything you write is encrypted in the database, and the operator sees no entries. Besides the password there is a second factor, and passkeys too. You see your signed-in devices and sign them out one by one.

sections.title: Your look
sections.body: Five colours, each light and dark, three layouts for Today, and the journal as a blog or a timeline. It applies to your account on every device.

small: Accounts by invitation, sign-in through authentik or another OpenID provider too.
Backups with upload and check, German and English, a log in four levels.
The app installs on the phone and takes texts from other apps.
